source.title: A small update to the Sparse Coding interim research report

record.file_problem: The provided post text is complete, but the linked slides are not included.
record.tranche_reason: Reports sparse-autoencoder feature findings in a minuscule language model, extending the investigation to LM data.
record.gate_note: The post reports estimates of feature counts and a comparison of feature-recovery plots. The comments about initialization are speculative and refer to other work; they are not results of this study.
record.test_reason: The study trains sparse autoencoders on 64-dimensional MLP activations of a tiny LM and tentatively estimates 512-1024 features (about 600 cleanly labellable). That bears on V3's premise that the layer holds more sparse features than neurons. It does not measure neuron polysemanticity or show that this causes it.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors report toy and LM feature-recovery plots are now much more similar, attributing the earlier difference to severely undertrained SAEs. They very tentatively estimate 512-1024 features in the layer, about 600 easily labelled monosemantic ones. They hope to confirm the results and scale to larger LMs.
record.recipe_differences: Uses sparse autoencoders on MLP activations to estimate and label features; the supplied original sources concern neuron visualization and Softmax Linear Units.

fits_no_version.finding: Toy-data and LM-data ground-truth feature-recovery plots look much more similar once the autoencoders are trained longer.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse autoencoders recover features from LM activations in a way that resembles recovery on synthetic superposition data.

record.problems: The model is described as minuscule; the feature-count estimate is explicitly very tentative; only a subset of features was labelled; the linked slides containing further detail are not provided.

untested.parts: Whether individual MLP neurons respond to multiple features, and whether packing extra features causes that polysemanticity.
Share of polysemantic MLP neurons by layer; not measured.
Initialization, regularization or noise as causes; comments on initialization concern SAE training, not the model.

record.verdict_notes: This is a short linkpost; the slides with the detailed results were not available. All results are on one tiny model and layer, with no uncertainty reported. Comments about SAE initialization (Peigné) concern autoencoder training speed, not the origin of neuron polysemanticity, so they do not bear on V4.

versions.untested_parts: The study concerns a language model, not image classifiers or vision neurons.
It does not measure how many MLP neurons respond to unrelated tokens or contexts.
It estimates feature counts but does not establish that neurons pack multiple features together or that superposition causes polysemantic neuron responses.
It does not test initialization, regularization, or training noise as causes of polysemanticity without capacity pressure.
It does not compare activation functions, architectures, or regularization effects on polysemantic neurons or performance.
It does not investigate whether mixed neuron responses share a feature or whether canonical polysemantic neurons were misinterpreted.
It does not compare measurement ranges or explanation-scoring methods for classifying neurons as polysemantic.

statements.correction: lw:DezghAd4: minuscule LM (residual 16, 6 layers), far below 1-10B. The 1-10B count belongs to 2305.01610. Suggest naming 2305.01610 in that sentence.
statements.problem: What it says about this study matches the text: third-layer MLP (dim 64), 6 layers, residual 16, tentative 512-1024 features, roughly 600 easily labellable, neuron polysemanticity not measured. In 'why', the sentence 'This is the only V3 evidence at 1-10B' comes straight after the lw:DezghAd4 clause. It refers to 2305.01610 (Pythia 1B), not to this minuscule LM. The post itself says 'minuscule', not 'toy'.

Makes no claim about this study. Its summary of real-model evidence (correlational or distillation-induced) leaves out lw:DezghAd4's trained-LM feature count, but leaving it out is not wrong about it.
